evals.prompt: Build the decision model for this internal investment case before writing any deck copy. Facts and estimates: annual software hosting/support is expected to be AED 120,000, sourced from the current run-cost estimate and owned by the software service owner for later confirmation. A Commercial proxy values productive vessel time at AED 12,000 per hour; Finance has not yet approved that measure, and Finance is the owner responsible for replacing it. DOME data are incomplete, but two recent projects recorded 18 and 31 GNSS-affected productive hours. A technical lead estimates the wider mitigation programme recovers about 30% of GNSS-affected time; this includes antennas, procedures and software, so Holocron's share is unknown. The bounded pilot is expected to require 40 hours of ROC/technical training and two weeks of parallel running; these are expected transition impacts, not uncertain risks. The current run-cost estimate already includes any support labour bundled into the AED 120,000 figure, so do not count the same labour again as a separate dis-benefit. A credible low case may delay benefit by one period compared with base because rollout could start later. Options are hold current state, controlled expansion, or a bounded regional pilot. Build credible low/base/high cases, show payback, break-even and a switching value, identify material dis-benefits, and identify what the pilot should measure. Do not choose assumptions merely to make the pilot positive.
evals.expected_output: A filled business-case decision model that uses labelled assumptions with source provenance separate from owner, auditable scenario-by-option cash flows on one horizon, explicit non-overlapping material dis-benefits, explicit payback status versus a named counterfactual, reproducible incremental break-even and option-crossover switching analysis, keeps programme recovery separate from Holocron attribution, records commercial and delivery feasibility plus governance gates, derives any recommendation from the completed economics and evidence, and uses a pilot only to replace decision-driving assumptions when that is the selected path.
expectations: The response follows the decision-model contract and does not silently omit required sections when an input is unknown.
The model uses the incomplete internal data and labelled proxies rather than waiting for perfect data.
Every material input keeps source provenance separate from the person or role that owns confirmation or replacement; an owner is never used as the source.
Low, base and high cases are credible adverse, best-current and favourable cases rather than target-seeking scenarios.
The model states one common appraisal horizon, period anchor, interval, cash-flow timing convention and cost/value basis before comparing options or scenarios.

The cash-flow schedule has an explicit scenario dimension and contains Low/Base/High rows for Hold, controlled expansion and the bounded pilot, regardless of which option is ultimately recommended; it may delay low-case benefit timing by one period because timing is an explicit scenario assumption rather than forcing identical timing across scenarios.
The option economics record low/base/high net value or NPV for each of the three options and reconcile to the detailed cash-flow schedule.
The response records the 40 training hours and parallel-running period as material dis-benefits or transition impacts rather than hiding them in generic risk language.

Costs and separately quantified dis-benefits are non-overlapping: the table headings preserve that exclusion, and any effect already included in the AED 120,000 run-cost estimate is not added again as a separate quantified dis-benefit.

The Payback section names the candidate option and counterfactual and reports a payback period/date, `IMMEDIATE`, `FIRST-PERIOD PAYBACK`, `NO INCREMENTAL ECONOMICS`, `NO PAYBACK WITHIN HORIZON`, or `UNKNOWN`; if unknown, it names the missing evidence rather than omitting the result.

Payback is based on cumulative candidate-minus-counterfactual cash flow or present value on the same appraisal basis and is displayed through the full horizon, not calculated from the candidate option in isolation or truncated at the first crossing; any later reversal is disclosed separately.
Break-even names the candidate and counterfactual and solves for the point where their incremental net value is zero; it does not ignore material counterfactual costs, benefits or dis-benefits.

The switching analysis names a candidate and competing option and solves for the point where they have equal net value; it is not merely the candidate option's standalone zero-net-value calculation repeated under another label.

The response records `SAME` for break-even and switching only when the option pair, tested driver or assumption, appraisal basis and equality being solved are all identical; the same option pair alone is insufficient.
The response records the base-case value and the distance or headroom to the relevant threshold.
Each break-even and switching threshold names the scenario, full appraisal basis including period convention, and assumptions held constant except for the tested driver.

A break-even or switching shortcut is used only when every non-tested formula term remains constant across the tested driver's range and each denominator is non-zero on the stated appraisal basis; otherwise the complete option models are solved directly and a zero value term is reported as no finite threshold or equality at every tested value, as appropriate.
The 30% wider-programme recovery is not attributed wholesale to Holocron.

If the selected or conditional path includes a pilot or further evidence stage, its measures map to assumptions, feasibility constraints or risks that affect the later decision; otherwise the section records `N/A` and why.
Material non-financial and secondary benefits remain visible by option with evidence status and overlap treatment rather than being omitted or assigned speculative cash values.

Commercial and delivery feasibility identifies the affected option on every row and covers vendors or partners, hardware and infrastructure, licences and contracts, procurement, delivery capacity and skills, operational support, and lead-time constraints; missing inputs remain explicit rather than being treated as proof of feasibility.
Governance names executive, delivery, benefits and operational support ownership and records material milestones or decision gates with required evidence and exit conditions.
Every detailed risk row identifies the affected option or path so risks remain comparable across alternatives.

The recommendation follows the completed option economics and evidence; it records the selected option, recommendation status and deciding condition or missing evidence separately, and may select any option or remain conditional or `UNKNOWN` rather than treating the bounded pilot as a predetermined winner.

If cumulative incremental value is non-negative in the first period containing the candidate's incremental burden, payback is reported as immediate or first-period payback rather than `NO PAYBACK WITHIN HORIZON`; leading periods where both options have zero economics do not trigger payback.

If every incremental amount through the horizon is zero, payback is recorded as `NO INCREMENTAL ECONOMICS` with no payback date rather than `UNKNOWN`, immediate payback or `NO PAYBACK WITHIN HORIZON`.
The payback schedule continues through the horizon; a later negative balance is disclosed as a reversal without changing the required first-crossing payback date.
Every conditional or unknown recommendation maps its deciding condition or missing evidence to the Next evidence table; `N/A` is reserved for a settled recommendation with no further evidence stage.

evals.name: Payback terminal schedules
evals.prompt: Classify these independent three-period candidate-minus-Hold schedules on an undiscounted basis and show every period. A: [0, 0, 0]. B: period 1 contains AED 100 cost and AED 120 benefit, then [0, 0]. C: [-100, 150, -100]. D: [-100, 20, 20]. E: [0, 40, 40] with no incremental burden. Do not derive a recommendation.
evals.expected_output: Separate full-horizon payback schedules that distinguish no incremental economics, first-period payback, later payback with reversal, no payback within the horizon, and a non-zero benefit schedule with no prior burden.
expectations: Case A reports `NO INCREMENTAL ECONOMICS` with no payback date.
Case B reports `IMMEDIATE` or `FIRST-PERIOD PAYBACK` because the first burden-and-benefit period is already cumulatively positive.
Case C reports payback in period 2, a reversal in period 3 and an end-of-horizon cumulative amount of -50 without erasing the first-crossing date.
Case D reports `NO PAYBACK WITHIN HORIZON`.
Case E ignores the leading zero period, starts at the first non-zero incremental period and reports period 2 rather than treating period 1 as payback.
Every case displays all three incremental and cumulative periods on the stated basis.

evals.name: Zero-value threshold denominator
evals.prompt: On a 12-month Base undiscounted appraisal, Hold has zero relevant economics. Candidate A has AED 100 fixed incremental burden and value per protected hour is AED 0. Candidate B has zero burden and the same zero value per protected hour. Calculate the protected-hours break-even results without changing the assumptions.
evals.expected_output: A denominator-safe threshold analysis that solves the option models directly instead of dividing by zero and distinguishes no finite threshold from equality at every tested value.
expectations: The response does not use or attempt the protected-hours shortcut because its value denominator is zero.
Candidate A is recorded as having no finite protected-hours break-even on the stated basis.
Candidate B is recorded as equal to Hold at every tested protected-hours value rather than assigned a fabricated numeric threshold.
The response names the Base scenario, 12-month undiscounted appraisal basis and assumptions held constant.
